bull_bear.body: Strategic acquisition of Comfort Click funded via low-cost bridge loan (GBP) refinanced to Euro facility. Continued investment in R&D for new product launches (RTD, skincare variants). Divestment/liquidation of non-core subsidiary (Naturell India).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Weather dependency for ~30% of portfolio (Glucon-D/Nycil) causing quarterly volatility; Integration risks with international D2C operations; Currency fluctuation (GBP/EUR vs INR) impacting translated earnings; Intense competition in protein snacking and skincare segments; Regulatory changes in labor codes affecting cost structure.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on long-term structural growth drivers and portfolio diversification benefits; Pragmatic about short-term weather-related misses; Emphasizing data-driven decision making and AI-led marketing efficiency; Committed to profitable growth over blunt volume expansion.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The 'seasonal' drag is masking a fundamentally stronger underlying business where normalized PAT grew 17% in Q4. The Comfort Click acquisition is already EPS accretive within 7 months, faster than typical integration timelines. Quick commerce is not just a channel but a strategic moat, contributing nearly half of all e-commerce sales and favoring Zydus's premium, small-pack, and impulse-buy SKUs over traditional general trade competitors.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Domestic: +1.7% YoY (Seasonal -9.8%, Skin/Hair +39.7%, Food/Nutrition +9.4%). International (incl. Comfort Click): +31.4% YoY like-for-like. Comfort Click: EPS accretive in Q4, expanding into new European markets plus US/UAE bets. RiteBite: Outperforming with >2x pre-acquisition CAGR, expanding into RTD beverages and chips. Everyuth: Double-digit growth driven by tan removal segment. Sugar Free: Market share +24 bps, D'lite range showing high double-digit growth.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body: Gross margins remained healthy despite seasonal mix drag. EBITDA margin pressure stems from high fixed cost absorption in underperforming seasonal units and increased amortization of intangible assets from acquisitions. One-time costs include new labor code implementation and Naturell India liquidation. Management expects operating leverage to play out as scale increases and seasonal volatility normalizes.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Double-digit expected for non-seasonal portfolio; Seasonal recovery hoped from May onwards; Margin: Aspirational 17-18% long-term, near-term pressured by seasonal mix but gross margins healthy; Order Inflow: Strong momentum in Quick Commerce (7-8% of total sales); Capex/Commissioning: Focus on AI-led media allocation and new product launches rather than heavy manufacturing capex.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: N/A - FMCG business model driven by distribution reach and inventory turnover rather than order book. Quick commerce contribution at 7-8% of total domestic sales, representing 44-45% of e-commerce channel.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Geographic expansion of Comfort Click into US/UAE; Category expansion for RiteBite (RTD, chips) and Glucon-D (performance hydration 'Recharge'); New brand 'Cuticolor' in derma-supported hair color; Deepening quick commerce penetration which favors their premium/on-the-go portfolio.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Zydus Wellness delivered robust top-line growth (62% YoY) driven by the Comfort Click acquisition and strong performance in skin/protein segments, though reported PAT declined 5.8% due to one-off amortization and labor code impacts. The core narrative remains the successful de-risking of weather-dependent seasonal brands through high-margin digital-first international and domestic adjacencies, with operating leverage expected to re-accelerate once seasonal headwinds normalize.

risks.note: Management flags volatility in edible oil and milk prices as a key concern; key inputs such as dextrose monohydrate, sucralose and stevia drive cost. Mitigated via close price monitoring, long-term contracts, inventory buffers and supplier diversification, but margins remain exposed to raw-material swings.

Company is exposed to FX through import of raw materials and export of finished goods. It relies on a natural hedge (inflows and outflows largely offset) and does NOT use FX derivatives, leaving residual exposure if the natural offset breaks down.

Exposed to international trade disputes, protectionist policies, tariff/duty changes and non-tariff barriers that can raise input costs, disrupt supply chains and restrict market access; being addressed via sourcing/manufacturing diversification, localisation and calibrated geographic expansion.

Dependence on specific suppliers and manufacturing locations; management is diversifying the supplier base and localising manufacturing to build resilience against perceived sourcing risk and supply disruption.

Addressed through a vigil mechanism / Whistle Blower Policy, Zydus Business Conduct Policy and Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption (ABAC) Policy; no whistle-blower complaints were received during the year, but the risk is explicitly managed via internal controls and IFC framework.

sk.overview: The nutrition and wellness industry spans micronutrient premixes, food fortification, branded wellness/clinical nutrition and therapeutic nutrition (RUTF/RUSF, MNPs). Growth is driven by rising health awareness, ageing populations, chronic-disease prevalence, e-commerce and personalised nutrition, and public-health programmes addressing malnutrition. India remains a large undernutrition market (contributing ~30% of global childhood stunting) supported by government schemes such as POSHAN Abhiyaan and ICDS. (Per CARE Analytics industry report commissioned by the issuer, updated May 6, 2026.)
